bug_info.bug_desc: In the LCI FSM escalation override, the terminal-error error code assignment was gated on `state_q != ErrorSt` instead of `error_q == NoError`. If escalation becomes active while the FSM is in WriteSt or WriteWaitSt after an OTP error has already been latched, the escalation block overwrites the recorded `error_q` with `FsmStateError`. The spec requires escalation to retain an already-recorded error code and only set the illegal-control-state error when no error has been recorded. This causes `error_o` to report the wrong persistent error code, losing the original OTP programming error.
bug_info.fix_hint: Change the escalation condition for setting `error_d = FsmStateError` to test `error_q == NoError` rather than `state_q != ErrorSt`. This preserves any previously latched OTP error while still setting the illegal-control-state error when escalation occurs with a clean error register.
